title: ReplayStrategist cannot replay the shadow role, so llm-shadow runs cannot be replayed (invariant 6)
description: The replay index is built only from `strategy.proposal` and `strategy.proposal_failed` records. StrategyScheduler.Handle logs successful shadow answers as `strategy.shadow` (DecisionRecordKinds.ShadowProposal), never as `strategy.proposal`. `new ReplayStrategist(records, ProposalRole.Shadow)` therefore loads only the shadow's failures. Every successful shadow request becomes a miss that answers null immediately and is logged as `no_opinion`. The replayed log loses all `strategy.shadow` records and its hash differs. The llm-shadow arm (spec step 4) is exactly the arm where the LLM is the shadow, so it cannot be replayed from its decision log, even though the spec and the class docs promise that it can, byte-identically.
failure_scenario: Demonstrated with a temporary test. Setup: BotRuntime with a synchronous primary and shadow = DelayedStrategist(40), 60 s, 10 s cadence. The recorded run has 4 `strategy.shadow` records. The replay with ReplayStrategist(recorded.Records, ProposalRole.Shadow) gives Recorded=2 (failures only), Misses=4, 0 `strategy.shadow` records, and a different hash.
suggested_fix: When role == Shadow, also index DecisionRecordKinds.ShadowProposal records. They already carry requestVersion, requestFrame, intent, cost and rawResponse. Add a shadow-replay case next to Recorded_llm_run_replays_identically_from_its_decision_log.

title: Shadow proposals skip the scheduler's late-discard check, so a result overtaken by a severe event is logged as wouldBe=Activated
description: Handle validates and previews Shadow-role results and returns before the invariant-2 check (`age > MaxProposalAgeSeconds` or `request.Invalidator`). The validator catches age itself (stale.snapshot), but its stale.event check only sees the current frame's events. A severity ≥0.7 event recorded in `request.Invalidator` on an earlier frame is therefore ignored for shadow results. The `strategy.shadow` record, which is the step-4 evidence of what the LLM would have done, then reports accepted=true and wouldBe=Activated for a proposal the primary path would have late-discarded. Shadow-vs-live comparisons overstate how often the LLM's advice would have been applied.
failure_scenario: Demonstrated with a temporary test. Setup: shadow = ControlledStrategist, requested at t=0. At t=2 a BaseUnderAttack event (0.9) arrives. At t=3 the shadow completes. The record says `accepted:true, wouldBe:Activated, wouldBeReason:yield` and LateDiscarded stays 0. The same sequence on the primary slot is late-discarded with reason `event` (existing test Severe_event_after_the_request_discards_the_result).
suggested_fix: Run the same age/Invalidator check for shadow requests and log `wouldBe = late:<reason>` (or a `late` field) in the shadow record instead of previewing arbitration. Do not count these in LateDiscarded, so the live metrics stay unchanged.

title: Base-threat override is level-triggered: every proposal during a sustained threat bypasses commitment and posture hysteresis
description: Decide activates any challenger with reason override:base_threat whenever BaseThreatRatio > 1.5 right now. It does not check whether the incumbent was itself installed by that same threat, or whether the incumbent is already a defensive plan (the class doc says "a threat the active plan was not built for"). The posture confidence margin is skipped too. Only the replan request is edge-detected, not the override. For as long as the threat lasts, commitment and hysteresis are both off.
failure_scenario: Confirmed with a probe. allied-boom is active at t=0. With a base threat of ratio 2.0 from t=5, primary proposals alternating generic-defend(Defend) and allied-boom(Boom) at 1 s intervals, each with confidence 0.1, are all Activated:override:base_threat. The result is 6 activations in 6 s and metrics.PostureFlips = 6. An LLM that wavers under attack flips the posture (and so production, budget and squads) every cadence while the base is under attack.
suggested_fix: Treat the override as consumed once used. Allow at most one override activation per threat episode, e.g. record the time or version of the activation that answered the threat. After that the new incumbent gets its normal commitment window (or a shorter override commitment). Skip the override when the incumbent is already Defend/Turtle, or when it was activated after the threat began.

title: A request still unanswered when the recording ends replays as an immediate no_opinion, so replayed logs grow extra tail records
description: When ProposeAsync finds no recorded answer it counts a miss and returns Task.FromResult(null). A request that was still in flight when the recorded match ended has a strategy.request record but no proposal or failure record. With 4 s of simulated LLM latency and a 5 s cadence, most llm+fast matches end with one such request. On replay that request completes at once, and the scheduler writes a strategy.proposal_failed no_opinion record the original never had. The replayed log is therefore never byte-identical, although every decision before the tail matches. That defeats the check "two runs are identical exactly when their hashes are".
failure_scenario: Demonstrated on the llm+fast arm with --llm-fake, rush, twin-valley, replayed as Primary with StrategicCadenceSeconds=5. Three of the four seeds shown differ only in the tail: seed 2 has 2180 recorded lines against 2181 replayed, Misses=1, first difference at line 2176, where the replay has {"kind":"strategy.proposal_failed","frame":17947,..."requestVersion":17948,"reason":"no_opinion"}. Seed 3: 1304 against 1305, first difference at 1300. Seed 4: 2176 against 2177, first difference at 2174. hashEqual=False in all three.
suggested_fix: Also index strategy.request records by role and version. When a request has a recorded strategy.request but no answer, treat it as pending forever, the same way a recorded timeout is treated, and do not answer null. Count a miss and answer null only for requests the recording never saw.

title: A firing abort trigger never ends the intent; if the fallback proposes the same playbook again, the aborted plan runs until it expires
description: When an abort trigger starts holding, Update() only sets FallbackRequested and ReplanRequested once, on the rising edge. Unlike expiry, it never calls End(). The incumbent is replaced only if a *different* playbook arrives. A re-proposal of the same playbook is refused as `abort_firing`, because it carries the same abort triggers. After that the edge has been consumed: abortFiring stays true, so nothing requests a fallback or replan again, and the planner keeps executing the aborted intent until ExpiresAt. The ProposalRole.Fallback doc says the fallback runs when the active intent 'aborted/expired', and the abort_firing rationale talks about 're-installing the very plan that just aborted'. Both assume an abort removes the plan, which it does not.
failure_scenario: Demonstrated with a temporary xunit test, since deleted. Primary installs allied-pressure with abort ArmyValueRatio<0.5. At t=40 own army is 300 against 1000. Update sets FallbackRequested. The fallback re-proposes allied-pressure and is Refused with reason abort_firing. Update is then called every second from t=41 to t=119 with the abort still holding. Active is still intent 'a', FallbackRequested=false and ReplanRequested=false. The same happens with the real selector and allied-harass. Its abort is LossesValue15s>=500. The selector picks allied-harass from sticky KnownTech air presence. So an Allied selector bot that is taking heavy losses keeps harassing for the rest of the 60 s lifetime.
suggested_fix: On the abort rising edge, end the intent (End(features, "aborted")) or at least mark it non-committable. Remember the aborted playbook and posture so that a re-proposal is refused and the fallback is re-asked until a different plan or the emergency intent is installed. Also keep requesting the fallback while the abort holds and no replacement has been accepted.

title: The ledger resets spending every period and sizes capacity from credits on hand, so on RA2 (charged while building) in-progress items are funded again
description: Every operational pass calls BeginPeriod. It clears `spent` and reservations and sets capacity to observed credits plus forecast income. The planner also checks each item only against `belief.Credits`. Neither counts the unpaid remainder of items already in production queues. The simulator debits the full cost at order time, so the problem does not appear there. RA2 debits gradually, as CommandGate's own remarks note, so observed credits stay almost unchanged after an order. The next pass, one second later, gets nearly the same capacity and spends it again on another queue. In accrual mode, Spend deducts the full cost from the pool balance, but the next Accrue sees capacity above the total and re-credits the spent amount across the pools by share. Invariant 4 (reservations never exceed credits plus one period of income) then holds only within a single 1 s period, not across the commitments actually outstanding.
failure_scenario: RA2 bridge, credits 2000. Pass 1 queues a 2000-credit war factory (ledger spent 2000). One second later credits read about 1950 because RA2 has charged only a little. BeginPeriod gives capacity about 1950 with spent=0. The now-idle vehicle queue gets a 900 tank, then the infantry queue a 200 unit. Outstanding commitments reach 3100 against 2000 credits. RA2 splits the money across queues, so every queue stalls, the intent's budget shares are not honoured, and the planner's 'saving' logic never triggers.
suggested_fix: Subtract outstanding commitments before sizing the period: Σ cost × (1 − Progress) over non-ready queue items, or a ledger-side list of committed-but-unpaid orders keyed by queue that is cleared when the item completes or is cancelled. Use the same figure for the planner's `credits`.

title: A stale or overtaken in-flight request holds the only primary slot until the 60 s timeout, so event-driven replans wait up to a minute
description: Only one primary request can be in flight at a time. Poll frees the slot only when the task completes or StrategistTimeoutSeconds (60 s) passes. A request whose result is already certain to be thrown away is not cancelled. This covers a request past MaxProposalAgeSeconds (15 s) and one whose Invalidator was set by a severity >= 0.7 event (MarkInvalidatingEvents). Meanwhile the major-event trigger waits in pendingTrigger. The proposal requires strategic planning on a 10-30 s cadence plus major events, and the spec requires freshness. In practice a slow or hung LLM leaves the bot with no strategic response to a base attack for up to 60 s. The replacement answer would still be discarded as late.

suggested_fix: In Poll, cancel an incomplete request once it can no longer be applied: when request.Invalidator is not null, or when now - SnapshotTime > MaxProposalAgeSeconds. Log proposal.failed with reason 'superseded' and free the slot, so the pending trigger starts a fresh request on the same tick. Keep StrategistTimeoutSeconds only as a backstop.
